entries.title: Isaiah 46:1
segments:
Bel-Nebo; Babylonian gods. 
 
  Boweth down--stoopeth; under the conqueror.  The gods of Babylon have gone into captivity with their worshippers. 
 
  Their idols; the images of Bel and Nebo. 
 
  Carriages; that is, things carried, loads; the old English sense of the word. 
 
  Heavy-laden; literally, "lifted up," placed upon the beasts.  The images of your gods, which you have been accustomed to bear in solemn procession, are now packed upon beasts to be carried away.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:2
segments:
They; the gods. 
 
  The burden; the load consisting of their own images.  Bel and Nebo cannot save their own images from this disgrace. 
 
The gods of the heathen need the constant care and protection of their makers.  They cannot help themselves, much less their worshippers.  So the objects to which worldly men give their supreme love and confidence--riches, honors, titles, pleasures--cannot save their possessors, but must themselves be watched over day and night, lest they "make themselves wings," and "fly away as an eagle toward heaven."

entries.title: Isaiah 46:3
segments:
vv 3-4. 
 
  Borne--carried; the gods of the heathen must be borne by their worshippers, but Jehovah bears and carries his people. 
 
  From the womb--to hoar hairs; from the infancy of Israel to his old age; that is through his whole existence.  See note to

. 
 
The salvation of nations, as well as of individual men, comes from God alone.  When they depart from him and put their trust in vanity and lies, they must perish.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:8
segments:
This; the contrast between Jehovah and the idol-gods. 
 
  Show yourselves men; act like men, not like children, as do the worshippers of idols.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:9
segments: The former things of old; ancient prophecies that have been fulfilled.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:11
segments: A ravenous bird; Cyrus, represented as a bird of prey.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:13
segments: Righteousness; as manifested in the deliverance of my people, and the destruction of their enemies.
